properties.article_text_excerpt: The European Commission said on Saturday it was closely monitoring the crisis surrounding Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, following a confrontation outside the court building on Friday night that was broadcast live on television. The incident has brought renewed attention to a dispute that has been ongoing for more than a decade.“It is for the Polish authorities to ensure that the Constitutional Tribunal can function in accordance with the Polish constitution and in respect of the relevant case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union,” a Commission spokesperson told Euronews on Saturday.“The appointment of eight new members of the Constitutional Tribunal lies within the constitutional power of the Sejm, Poland’s parliament,” the spokesperson added.The Commission spokesperson also pointed to a ruling by the European Court of Human Rights, which on 5 May 2026 issued interim measures requiring the competent Polish authorities “to refrain from hindering the taking up and exercise of judicial duties by judges appointed by the Sejm in March 2026”.Tusk: “Restoring calm does not mean accepting lawlessness”Prime Minister Donald Tusk addressed Poles in a televised speech on Satur

Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP View image in fullscreen Donald Trump in the Oval Office, Washington DC, 5 November 2026. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP Opinion Donald Trump Donald Trump’s power is on the wane. What next for Russia, Israel – and the rest of us? Simon Tisdall With the global tide turning against him, the US president’s lame duck status could still aggravate old tensions and spark new explosions Sun 8 Nov 2026 01.00 EST Last modified on Sun 8 Nov 2026 10.23 EST Share I t was a victory for the world, too. People in the many countries that suffered pain, loss and cruel indignities at the hands of Donald Trump over the past two chaotic, fearful years celebrated a moment of glorious, shared redemption. The monster, like others of his kind, still lurks in his gilded White House lair; far-right authoritarianism still casts a dark shadow over many nations. But the power of this most destructive of presidents is shattered , his malignant spell broken. The triumphant roar of US midterm voters was a rallying cry of democratic defiance that, echoing the American revolution of 250 years ago, reverberated around the globe.

Photograph: Megan Varner/Pool Reuters/AP G20 US cancels G20 ‘family photo’ after Australia, UK and others refuse to appear with Russia Marco Rubio pulls plug on traditional photo op at meeting of foreign ministers after about one-third of countries threaten boycott Ben Doherty and Associated Press Fri 30 Oct 2026 20.29 EDT Last modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 22.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The traditional “family photo” to open the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting has been abruptly cancelled in the US after a host of nations – including Australia and the UK – refused to appear beside the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, pulled the plug after several European officials, the UK and Australia made it known they would boycott or walk out of the snapshot that often kicks off such international gatherings. What we know on day 1,708 Guardian staff and agencies Tue 27 Oct 2026 21.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukrainian forces are retaking territory through a series of offensives , adding Kyiv’s battlefield ⁠position was the strongest it had been ⁠in some ​time. The Ukrainian president, citing ⁠a report by senior commanders, noted for the first time the “Veles” operation using pipelines in Ukraine’s northeast. He also referred to an air assault operation in ⁠eastern Ukraine and the “Vivaldi” operation further to the north, designed to prevent Russian advances in ​key areas.
